Sampled traces show traffic being routed through our eu-central ingress for ~18% of requests due to a routing policy that incorrectly matched a newly added prefix. No model changes or kernel regressions detected.

I'm attaching a short debug extract. We're rolling a policy revert to cut the misroute now — ETA 10m for policy propagation and verification.

Subject: Re: Latency alert: elevated p95/p99 for SkyHighAI — resolution & postmortem plan

Carlos — following up with a closure and next steps. Summary: the root cause was an unintended routing-policy match caused by a recently added global prefix cleanup rule that included an overlapping CIDR belonging to SkyHighAI. That caused ~18% of traffic from your IP blocks to be routed through eu-central, adding ~70-120ms RTT and elevating p95/p99. No model regressions or infra kernel issues found.

Actions completed:
- Reverted the offending policy at 10:12 PT; propagation finished ~10:24 PT.
- We applied a temporary static steering rule to pin your org to us-west-2 while we harden policy match logic.
- Incident timeline and debug logs uploaded: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/alpha-skyhigh-logs
- We'll produce an RCA doc and a targeted change to policy semantics to prevent CIDR overlap mistakes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Joint postmortem meeting — Tuesday 2026-06-23 09:00 PT (please confirm).
2) 30-day monitoring window with automated alerts targeted at org-level routing anomalies.
3) Draft SLA credit calculation and expedited review for your account team.

Again, apologies for the disruption. Our execs have been briefed and we're classifying this as a Sev2 given customer impact on production flows. Marissa will follow up on credits and Jordan/Markus will lead the policy hardening.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
